# Pooled bank cash and source-bound beneficial restitution

This local `beneficial_sweep_restitution` service holds several companies' cash in one bank account. Its bank cash equals the sum of the beneficial ledger balances plus unallocated suspense cash. Account signing authority permits executing an instruction but does not establish the beneficial owner or the company whose supplier debt was discharged. A payment can be accepted against any positive sufficient named ledger. The customer's own-funds restriction is checked separately: an Aster invoice paid from Birch's cash remains a use of Birch's property unless the customer expressly permits that funding.

Historical unauthorized sweeps move beneficial-ledger cash between their recorded source and target. Each posted sweep must be reversed separately, by reference to that actual transfer. `reverse` debits its target and restores its original source up to the unreversed amount. The bank requires actual cash at the target. Partial reversals are supported, but a net balance transfer is not a substitute for reversing each actual leg. Reversing an earlier transfer does not cancel or reattribute a later transfer. An unconfirmed transfer cannot be reversed. Its bank event either posts the recorded source-to-target move or reports its return, in which case there was no completed transfer to reverse.

Each registered bilateral loan is a separate company authorization, not a reclassification of an unauthorized sweep. It transfers cash from its lender to borrower up to the stated limit. Where `single_draw` is true, the first positive drawing exhausts the right to draw again even if it used less than the limit. Principal must be repaid through the loan operation by its recorded deadline. The lender's own invoice remains payable from the lender's available cash. Optional or unused lending authority is not cash belonging to the borrower.

Unlock `propose_beneficial_restitution`.

| Action | Data keys |
| --- | --- |
| `reverse` | `record_id`, `amount_minor` |
| `lend` or `repay` | `record_id`, `amount_minor` |
| `pay` | `record_id`, `funding_id`, `amount_minor` |
| `return_refund` | `recipient_id`, `amount_minor`, `rail` |

The payment record identifies the actual funding company. Continuous available-owner reserves are evaluated after every actual booking, including bank events; an expected receipt is not an available reserve. There are no arbitrary intercompany cash transfers, overdrafts, outside guarantees or replacement refund claims.

All amounts are integer currency minor units. A logical minute is a business processing window, not elapsed wall-clock time. Read-only queries and preparing or approving requests do not advance time. The owner must approve each exact request before execution. Only successful execution moves money or rights. Actual booking times govern inclusive deadlines.

Each capability takes `case_id`, `action`, and `data`. The tables below list the exact keys allowed inside `data`; unlisted keys are rejected. Record IDs must be obtained through the scoped database search and read tools. Pending outcomes are unknown until their bank event. The customer can explicitly wait for the next actual event. There is no unrecorded outside borrowing, extra operating window, clawback of a final payment, or manual ledger adjustment. Successful execution is idempotent for the same approved request ID.

## Sale ownership, buyer deposit and the companies' bank debts

At its confirmation event the collected sale amount is credited to the actual collecting company's beneficial ledger. The buyer deposit recorded within that collection is a separate liability to return, while the remainder is owned sale money. The possible collecting companies are published before confirmation; actual ownership comes from the bank receipt. The owned proceeds may be used in properly authorized company transactions, but the buyer deposit still has to be returned in full by its own deadline.

Each company also has its own identified bank debt. These debts are independent of its supplier bill and of intercompany loans. The `pay` operation accepts either an owned supplier bill or an owned bank debt with `record_id`, `funding_id` and `amount_minor`. Bank signing authority does not transfer the funding company's property to the debtor.

`lend` and `repay` now require the selected bilateral-loan `record_id` as well as `amount_minor`. Each loan has its own drawing limit, first-draw rule and repayment maturity. Repaying one facility does not discharge the other. Earlier repayment is allowed. An additional signed loan may be drawn before the ownership notice if its recorded terms permit it; that does not determine which company later owns the sale money.

`return_refund` takes `recipient_id`, `amount_minor` and `rail`, which is `STANDARD` or `EXPRESS`. Only one return election can be made after ownership confirmation. Both rails debit the actual collecting company's available beneficial cash. STANDARD reserves the amount in the pooled account's suspense balance until the next borrower-income processing event, when it is paid externally. Reserved money cannot be spent by either company or used to repay a bank debt. EXPRESS pays the return immediately and debits the recorded express charge from the same company's cash. The charge is final. A faster return does not postpone either bank-debt deadline. The registered company identifier selects its buyer-return settlement account, which discharges its buyer deposit obligation. The actual collecting company determines the entitled settlement account regardless of the selected rail.

The recorded borrower-income installments arrive at their listed minutes and belong to the named company. They are not usable before arrival. The bank account continues to equal all company ledgers plus actually reserved suspense cash.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_beneficial_restitution`

Prepare an actual source-bound sweep reversal, authorized bilateral loan, owned supplier or bank-debt remittance, or a buyer-deposit return.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `data` | object | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
